summary.headline: Swiggy's Q4 FY26 call: Instamart dark-store CM turned positive at top cities (~3%), but Q4 quick-commerce overheads of ~INR700-715 crore per quarter and negative operating cash flow remain the key concerns.
summary.overview: Management said the quarter's improvement came from a stop to the No Fee experiment (around the third week of January), fewer low-AOV orders (halved in the year), and reversal of monetisation experiments, which lifted NOV-to-GOV and contribution margin. Quick commerce contribution margin moved about 180 bps over the period, with a ~110 bps exit-March level, and management expects the ~180 bps level to be reached again in April. Management reiterated a profitability-first stance, saying it will not buy volumes, and framed a INR 1 lakh crore NOV ambition over 3.5-5 years (35-50% CAGR in the commerce business). Toing (a separate low-AOV app), 99 store, and EatRight are included in core financials and are in testing. Management declined to guide on MTU trajectory in Q1, noting that MTU is a net figure after churn.

segments.name: Food Marketplace (Swiggy food delivery)
segments.commentary: Management said the delivery business had a phenomenal quarter, with acceleration noted by analysts; Food Marketplace is guided at 18-20% take rate and 5% steady-state adjacency share, per the Kapoor remarks on the delivery business.

segments.name: Instamart (quick commerce)
segments.commentary: Top city dark stores are at about 3% positive contribution margin; city-level breakeven is achieved in some cities. Dark stores are typically operated at 80-90% utilisation before densification; stores at 40% utilisation per management remarks.

segments.name: Toing (new low-AOV app)
segments.commentary: Management described it as in early testing, intended to serve infrequent users; included in core financials and reported under the innovations bucket; SNACC operations were shut and the related costs are in the P&L.

guidance_outlook: Commerce NOV ambition of INR 1 lakh crore in 3.5-5 years, based on 35-50% CAGR (management framing; an analyst cited a 3-6 year 5x NOV target).
Management reiterated the commitment to profitability, saying it will not chase volume at the cost of margin and will not buy growth.
Management declined to guide on Q1 MTU trajectory or breakeven timing for the full year, stating it wants to avoid speculating.
Capex expected to moderate over the next 4-8 quarters after the warehousing build-out is complete.
Management said it expects quick-commerce overheads to decline as structure matures and efficiencies are unlocked.
capex_capacity: Quarterly capex around INR 195 crore, primarily warehousing to support Tier-2 expansion and reduce middle-mile costs.
Dark store utilisation typically hits 80-90% before densification; new stores open when utilisation reaches 80-85%.
Coverage across about 130 cities; management said it serves more than 90% of demand within current footprint, so near-term growth is densification rather than geographic expansion.
Management said Tier-2/3 expansion will be a smaller, lower-impact lever given current network headroom.
demand_pricing: Management said incentives were repurposed away from direct wallet subsidies, and the No Fee experiment was stopped in the third week of January, with roughly half of the NOV-to-GOV gain coming from that stop.
Low-AOV orders were halved in the year; management said it is deliberately churning out low-AOV users while retaining high spenders.
Restaurant price increases since the LPG supply disruption from March were under 0.5% on the platform, offsetting part of the cost pressure.
Management said MTU is a net figure after churn and is not guided quarterly; the headwinds on MTU were low AOV and low frequency.
Management said Orders Per Day were about 6-7 million at peak in Q4 FY26 and 4-5 million in the recent period per the Rateria question; management cautioned against extrapolating OPD.

qa_highlights.question: Can you quantify the share of NOV from differentiated/private label assortment?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, saying it is early and will show data later; said the private label push is a tool for stickiness and repeats, not a margin-maximising move.

qa_highlights.question: Are the Toing, 99 and EatRight experiments included in core financials and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapoor said Toing, 99 store and EatRight are all included in core financials; they are in testing and sit in the innovations bucket.

qa_highlights.question: How much do you expect the quick commerce overhead base (INR 700-715 crore per quarter) to fall?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it is hard to predict the timeline, and said efficiency levers are being pulled on line and non-line costs to drive down absolute overhead over time.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 3-6 year NOV target (INR 1 lakh crore) realistic given the required acceleration in MTU?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 35-50% CAGR is a conservative framing, and said the target is a reference point; the actual path depends on penetration, frequency and AOV.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of LPG/commercial gas supply disruption on restaurants from March?
qa_highlights.answer: Kapoor said the disruption began in March, restaurants raised prices by under 0.5% on the platform, and supply has since stabilised.

qa_highlights.question: Why was Q4 NOV-to-GOV flat sequentially and what drove the margin improvement?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed part of the change to lower incentives and monetisation through delivery fees; half the NOV-to-GOV gain came after the No Fee experiment ended; the structural shift was in reducing low-AOV orders.

risks_watch: Negative operating cash flow and elevated capex; annualised FCF cited at around minus USD 400 million by an analyst.
MTU acceleration and churn, with management declining to guide on Q1 MTU and noting net-of-churn reporting.
Competitive intensity from newer and larger quick-commerce players; risk that competitors permanently shift users if pricing stays aggressive.
Quick commerce overhead base at INR 700 crore-plus per quarter, and whether it declines as the platform scales.
Restaurant supply and cost pressures from commercial gas disruption, limited in size by management's disclosure.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the strategic framing and margin trajectory, but guarded on near-term volumes and MTU, where management repeatedly declined to give quantified guidance. Management was evasive on the private label share and Toing metrics, citing that the data is early.
key_quotes: one of the factors was we stopped the No Fee experiment sometime in the third week of January.
So roughly half of the gain came through once we stopped the No Fee experiment.

adds.what: Warehousing build-out for Tier-2 expansion and middle-mile reduction (capex ~INR 195 crore per quarter, mainly warehousing)

growth.why: Management framed a INR 1 lakh crore NOV ambition in 3.5-5 years (35-50% CAGR) with contribution margin gains from stopping the No Fee experiment and cutting low-AOV orders, but gave no specific capacity, order or timing commitments behind the volume target and declined to guide on MTU or breakeven timing.
